title: Statistics - Lesson 5: Box-and-Whisker Plots Assessment
description: Assessment for constructing, reading, and interpreting box-and-whisker plots.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of a box-and-whisker plot?
options: It summarizes center and spread using the five-number summary.
It lists every data value in its original order.
It shows the exact frequency of each repeated value.
It converts all values into percentages.
questions.explanation: A box-and-whisker plot uses the minimum, Q1, median, Q3, and maximum to summarize center and spread.

questions.question: Order the data 18, 12, 30, 24, 16, 21. What is the minimum? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The ordered data are 12, 16, 18, 21, 24, 30, so the minimum is 12.

questions.question: For the ordered data 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, what is the median? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: There are seven values, so the fourth value, 9, is the median.

questions.question: For the ordered data 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, what are Q1 and Q3?
questions.explanation: Leave out the median 9. The lower half is 3, 5, 7, so Q1 = 5. The upper half is 11, 13, 15, so Q3 = 13.

questions.question: A five-number summary is 2, 7, 11, 15, 19. Which value is the median line inside the box?
questions.explanation: The third value in the five-number summary is the median, so the median line is at 11.

questions.question: The box in a box-and-whisker plot represents the middle 50% of the data.
questions.explanation: The box stretches from Q1 to Q3, which contains the middle half of the ordered data.

questions.question: A data set has Q1 = 14 and Q3 = 31. What is the IQR? Enter just the number.
Which five-number summary would produce the widest box?
questions.explanation: The box width is Q3 - Q1. The first option has IQR = 25 - 8 = 17, which is larger than the others.

questions.question: A longer whisker means that section of values is more spread out, not that it contains more data points.
questions.explanation: Each quartile section represents about 25% of the data, but the numerical distance can vary.

questions.question: A box plot has minimum 40, Q1 48, median 52, Q3 54, and maximum 70. Which interpretation is best?
options: The upper whisker is long, so the high values are more spread out.
The median is closer to the maximum than to Q1.
questions.explanation: The upper whisker runs from 54 to 70, which is much longer than the lower whisker from 40 to 48.

questions.question: Find the five-number summary for 6, 8, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20. Show the values in order.
questions.explanation: The data are ordered. The median is 12, the lower half is 6, 8, 9 so Q1 = 8, and the upper half is 15, 18, 20 so Q3 = 18.

questions.question: Explain why a box plot should be drawn on a scaled number line.
questions.correctAnswer: A scaled number line makes the distances match the data values, so the spread is shown accurately.
questions.explanation: Without a scale, a plot can exaggerate or hide differences in spread.

questions.question: Two classes have medians of 82 and 82. Class A has IQR 6, and Class B has IQR 18. What does this tell you?
questions.correctAnswer: The classes have the same median, but Class B's middle 50% is more spread out. Class A's middle scores are more consistent.
questions.explanation: Equal medians mean equal centers, while the larger IQR for Class B means greater spread in the middle half.

questions.question: A student says, "The right whisker is longer, so most of the data are on the right." Correct the statement.
questions.correctAnswer: A longer right whisker means the highest quarter of values is more spread out, not that most data are on the right.
questions.explanation: Box-plot sections represent quarters of the data. Length shows spread within that quarter.

questions.question: When constructing a box plot from the summary 10, 13.5, 20, 25, 30, where should the box be drawn?
questions.explanation: The box is drawn from Q1 to Q3, so it runs from 13.5 to 25.
